content:
We have many templates returned. Need one that matches our target molecule and corresponds to carbonyl-ene reaction (intramolecular). The target molecule: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

So it's a cyclohexane ring with OH and CF3 attached, plus an exocyclic alkene attached to aromatic phenyl? Actually [CH2]=[C] attached to aromatic phenyl and to chiral carbon bearing ring.

We need retrosynthetic step: break C=C to carbonyl? In carbonyl-ene, forward: alkene + carbonyl -> new C-C bond, forming allylic alcohol. Retrosynthesis: break C-C bond formed, generate carbonyl and alkene. So we need template that when applied to product (our molecule) gives precursors: an alkene and a carbonyl (ketone). The template likely has pattern: [C:...]-[C@...](...)-[OH] -> carbonyl + alkene.

Search results include template 1229769 etc. Look at its retro_smarts_template: '[C:5]-[C@;H0;D4;+0:6](-[C:7])(-[OH;D1;+0:8])-[C;H0;D4;+0:1](-[F;D1;H0:2])(-[F;D1;H0:3])-[F;D1;H0:4]>>C-[Si](-C)(-C)-[C;H0;D4;+0:1](-[F;D1;H0:2])(-[F;D1;H0:3])-[F;D1;H0:4].[C:5]-[C;H0;D3;+0:6](-[C:7])=[O;H0;D1;+0:8]'

This seems to be a protecting group removal (Si) and carbonyl formation. Not our case.

Template 1237522: retro_smarts: '[c:2]1:[cH;D2;+0:1]:[cH;D2;+0:4]:[c:5]:[cH;D2;+0:6]:[cH;D2;+0:3]:1>>C-C(=O)-c1:c:[cH;D2;+0:1]:[c:2]:[cH;D2;+0:3]:c:1.C-[C@]12-C-[C@H](-c3:c:[cH;D2;+0:4]:[c:5]:[cH;D2;+0:6]:c:3)-C3=C4-C-C-C5(-C=C-4-C-C-[C@@H]-3-[C@H]-1-C-C-C-2=O)-O-C-C-O-5'

Seems complex.

Template 1042412: retro_smarts: '[C:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[CH2;D1;+0:4])-[c:3]>>O=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[C:2])-[c:3].[CH3;D1;+0:4]-[Mg+]'

This is a carbonyl-ene? It breaks a C-C double bond to carbonyl and alkene? The forward reaction would be carbonyl + alkene -> C-C double bond? Actually retro: product has C-C double bond (C;H0;D3;+0:1)(=[CH2]) attached to C and aromatic c. It breaks to carbonyl O=C(-C)-c and CH3-Mg. Not ours.

We need a template where product has an allylic alcohol (C-OH) and a carbonyl broken. Look at template 1209837: retro_smarts '[C:3]-[C:2](-[C:4])-[OH;D1;+0:1]>>C-C(=C)-C(=O)-[O;H0;D2;+0:1]-[C:2](-[C:3])-[C:4]'

This seems to convert an alcohol attached to carbon chain into carbonyl and alkene. That matches carbonyl-ene: product is alcohol, precursors are carbonyl and alkene. Our product has OH on carbon attached to CF3 and ring. So template 1209837 may apply.

Let's try applying this template to our molecule to see if it matches. Use apply_template.
